claim: Toddler/Apela/Elabela is a conserved secreted peptide that regulates mesendoderm development during zebrafish gastrulation.
source: Toddler/Apela/Elabela is a conserved secreted peptide that regulates mesendoderm development during zebrafish gastrulation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about Toddler.

claim: The 'specification model' postulates that Toddler signaling enhances Nodal signaling to properly specify endoderm.
source: The 'specification model' postulates that Toddler signaling enhances Nodal signaling to properly specify endoderm
evidence: This describes one of the two models being tested in the study, citing previous work.

claim: The 'migration model' posits that Toddler signaling regulates mesendodermal cell migration downstream of Nodal signaling.
source: the 'migration model' posits that Toddler signaling regulates mesendodermal cell migration downstream of Nodal signaling.
evidence: This describes the alternative model being tested in the study.

claim: In toddler mutants, Nodal signaling is initially normal.
source: We find that in toddler mutants Nodal signaling is initially normal
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: Increasing endoderm specification does not rescue mesendodermal cell migration in toddler mutants.
source: increasing endoderm specification does not rescue mesendodermal cell migration
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figures 1 and 2.

claim: Mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants result from a decrease in animal pole-directed migration.
source: Mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants result from a decrease in animal pole-directed migration
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants are independent of endoderm.
source: Mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants result from a decrease in animal pole-directed migration and are independent of endoderm.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Endodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants are dependent on a Cxcr4a-regulated tether of the endoderm to mesoderm.
source: Conversely, endodermal cell migration defects are dependent on a Cxcr4a-regulated tether of the endoderm to mesoderm.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract and supported by data in Figure 7.

claim: Toddler signaling regulates mesodermal cell migration downstream of Nodal signaling.
source: These results suggest that Toddler signaling regulates mesodermal cell migration downstream of Nodal signaling
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study based on multiple experimental results.

claim: Toddler signaling indirectly affects endodermal cell migration via Cxcr4a-signaling.
source: These results suggest that Toddler signaling regulates mesodermal cell migration downstream of Nodal signaling and indirectly affects endodermal cell migration via Cxcr4a-signaling.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on experimental results in Figure 7.

claim: Gastrulation is a conserved process in embryogenesis during which the three germ layers undergo large-scale rearrangements to shape the embryo.
source: Gastrulation is a conserved process in embryogenesis during which the three germ layers – endoderm, mesoderm and ectoderm – undergo large-scale rearrangements to shape the embryo (Solnica-Krezel, 2005; Schier, 2009; Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Solnica-Krezel and Sepich, 2012).
evidence: This is background information supported by multiple citations.

claim: Following their specification, endoderm and mesoderm internalize beneath the ectoderm and migrate away from the site of internalization.
source: Following their specification, endoderm and mesoderm (jointly referred to as mesendoderm) internalize beneath the ectoderm and migrate away from the site of internalization.
evidence: This is background information about gastrulation movements.

claim: Defects in cellular movements during gastrulation can lead to a truncated body axis and abnormal organs.
source: Defects in these cellular movements can lead to a truncated body axis and abnormal organs, while defects in initial specification cause absence or reduction of mesendoderm derivatives (Solnica-Krezel, 2005; Schier, 2009; Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Solnica-Krezel and Sepich, 2012).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Defects in initial specification cause absence or reduction of mesendoderm derivatives.
source: Defects in these cellular movements can lead to a truncated body axis and abnormal organs, while defects in initial specification cause absence or reduction of mesendoderm derivatives (Solnica-Krezel, 2005; Schier, 2009; Langdon and Mullins, 2011; Solnica-Krezel and Sepich, 2012).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Endoderm and mesoderm specification depends on the TGFβ-ligand Nodal.
source: Endoderm and mesoderm specification depends on the TGFβ-ligand Nodal.
evidence: This is established background knowledge about germ layer specification.

claim: Secreted Nodal ligands bind to Activin receptors, which leads to Smad2 phosphorylation and target gene induction.
source: Secreted Nodal ligands bind to Activin receptors, which leads to Smad2 phosphorylation and target gene induction (Schier, 2009).
evidence: This is background information about Nodal signaling mechanism supported by citation.

claim: Nodal signals trigger transcription of their own inhibitors, which belong to the Lefty family.
source: Nodal signals also trigger transcription of their own inhibitors, which belong to the Lefty family.
evidence: This is background information about Nodal signaling regulation.

claim: lefty mutants have increased Nodal signaling resulting in increased endodermal and mesodermal gene expression and cell number during gastrulation.
source: Thus, lefty mutants have increased Nodal signaling resulting in increased endodermal and mesodermal gene expression and cell number during gastrulation (Meno et al., 1999; Rogers et al., unpublished ).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: After specification by Nodal, endodermal cells are tethered to mesodermal cells through a fibronectin-integrin link genetically regulated by the GPCR Cxcr4a.
source: After specification by Nodal, endodermal cells are tethered to mesodermal cells through a fibronectin-integrin link genetically regulated by the GPCR Cxcr4a (Mizoguchi et al., 2008; Nair and Schilling, 2008).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Loss of Cxcr4a releases the tether between endoderm and mesoderm and results in excessive animal pole-directed migration of endodermal cells.
source: Loss of Cxcr4a releases this tether and results in excessive animal pole-directed migration of endodermal cells, while mesodermal cell migration is unaffected (Mizoguchi et al., 2008; Nair and Schilling, 2008).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Mesodermal cell migration is unaffected by loss of Cxcr4a.
source: Loss of Cxcr4a releases this tether and results in excessive animal pole-directed migration of endodermal cells, while mesodermal cell migration is unaffected (Mizoguchi et al., 2008; Nair and Schilling, 2008).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Toddler/Apela/Elabela is required for proper endoderm and mesoderm formation and migration.
source: An additional GPCR pathway, regulated by Toddler/Apela/Elabela, is also required for proper endoderm and mesoderm formation and migration (Chng et al., 2013; Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Toddler is highly conserved throughout vertebrates.
source: In this pathway, the secreted peptide Toddler, which is highly conserved throughout vertebrates, signals via the GPCR APJ (in zebrafish: Apelin receptor A and B, jointly referred to as Apelin receptor).
evidence: This is background information about Toddler conservation.

claim: Toddler signals via the GPCR APJ (Apelin receptor A and B in zebrafish).
source: In this pathway, the secreted peptide Toddler, which is highly conserved throughout vertebrates, signals via the GPCR APJ (in zebrafish: Apelin receptor A and B, jointly referred to as Apelin receptor).
evidence: This is background information about Toddler signaling mechanism.

claim: In toddler mutants, initial specification of endoderm and mesoderm is normal.
source: In toddler mutants, initial specification of endoderm and mesoderm is normal (Pauli et al., 2014)
evidence: This is background information supported by citation.

claim: By mid-gastrulation, toddler mutants have fewer endodermal cells.
source: but by mid-gastrulation, toddler mutants have fewer endodermal cells and mesendodermal cell migration is reduced (Chng et al., 2013; Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Mesendodermal cell migration is reduced in toddler mutants by mid-gastrulation.
source: but by mid-gastrulation, toddler mutants have fewer endodermal cells and mesendodermal cell migration is reduced (Chng et al., 2013; Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: toddler mutants generally die around 7 days post fertilization with deformed hearts, blood accumulation, edema and endodermal abnormalities.
source: toddler mutants generally die around 7 days post fertilization (dpf) with deformed hearts, blood accumulation, edema and endodermal abnormalities (Chng et al., 2013; Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information about toddler mutant phenotypes supported by citations.

claim: Apelin receptor signaling has been proposed to enhance Nodal signaling.
source: Moreover, Apelin receptor signaling has been proposed to enhance Nodal signaling, possibly accounting for the endoderm cell number defects in toddler mutants (Deshwar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a claim from previous literature being tested in this study.

claim: Mesendodermal cells migrate more slowly during internalization in toddler mutants.
source: This model is supported by the observation that mesendodermal cells migrate more slowly during internalization in toddler mutants, and that apelin receptor a and b gene expression depend on Nodal signaling (Tucker et al., 2007; Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: apelin receptor a and b gene expression depend on Nodal signaling.
source: This model is supported by the observation that mesendodermal cells migrate more slowly during internalization in toddler mutants, and that apelin receptor a and b gene expression depend on Nodal signaling (Tucker et al., 2007; Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information supported by citations.

claim: Endodermal cell numbers are comparable between wild-type and toddler mutant embryos at 60% epiboly.
source: We found that endodermal cell numbers are comparable between wild-type and toddler mutant embryos at 60% epiboly
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Endodermal cells in wild-type and toddler mutants divide at similar rates.
source: and that they go on to divide at similar rates, suggesting that initial specification and subsequent proliferation are not affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)(Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Initial specification and subsequent proliferation of endoderm are not affected in toddler mutants.
source: and that they go on to divide at similar rates, suggesting that initial specification and subsequent proliferation are not affected (Figure 1—figure supplement 1)(Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is an inference based on the cell number and division rate data.

claim: toddler mutant embryos have increased rates of cell death, including endodermal cell death.
source: Instead, we found increased rates of cell death in toddler mutant embryos, including endodermal cell death, which may account for the decreased cell numbers observed during later gastrulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Increased cell death in toddler mutants may account for the decreased cell numbers observed during later gastrulation.
source: Instead, we found increased rates of cell death in toddler mutant embryos, including endodermal cell death, which may account for the decreased cell numbers observed during later gastrulation (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the cell death data.

claim: lefty2 single and toddler;lefty2 double mutant embryos had more endodermal cells than toddler single mutants and wild-type embryos.
source: As expected, lefty2 single and toddler;lefty2 double mutant embryos had more endodermal cells than toddler single mutants and wild-type embryos (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Endodermal cells in lefty2 single mutants migrated normally.
source: While endodermal cells in lefty2 single mutants migrated normally, endodermal cell dispersion in toddler;lefty2 double mutants was not rescued and resembled toddler single mutant siblings (Figure 1A,C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Endodermal cell dispersion in toddler;lefty2 double mutants was not rescued and resembled toddler single mutant siblings.
source: While endodermal cells in lefty2 single mutants migrated normally, endodermal cell dispersion in toddler;lefty2 double mutants was not rescued and resembled toddler single mutant siblings (Figure 1A,C and D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 1.

claim: Mesodermal cell dispersion was not rescued in toddler;lefty2 double mutants.
source: As with endoderm, mesodermal cell dispersion was not rescued in toddler;lefty2 double mutants (Figure 2A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 2.

claim: Increasing endodermal cell number did not rescue the endodermal or mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants.
source: Thus, increasing endodermal cell number did not rescue the endodermal or mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the toddler;lefty2 double mutant data.

claim: Hearts in toddler;lefty2 double mutants resembled toddler single mutants, except in rare cases when hearts were wild-type in size.
source: Hearts in toddler;lefty2 double mutants resembled toddler single mutants, except in rare cases when hearts were wild-type in size (Figure 2C–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: By 3 dpf, toddler;lefty2 double mutant larvae had similar or more severe patterning defects as compared to their toddler single mutant siblings.
source: By 3 dpf, toddler;lefty2 double mutant larvae had similar or more severe patterning defects as compared to their toddler single mutant siblings (Figure 2E–F).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 2E-F.

claim: Increasing endoderm cell number cannot rescue toddler mutant phenotypes.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that increasing endoderm cell number cannot rescue toddler mutant phenotypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the toddler;lefty2 double mutant data.

claim: Wild-type and toddler mutant embryos show no difference in expression of lefty1 and lefty2 just before gastrulation.
source: First, we used in situ hybridization to examine expression of two direct Nodal target genes, lefty1 and lefty2, just before gastrulation and found no difference between wild-type and toddler mutant embryos (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 3A.

claim: apelin receptor a and b single and double mutants displayed normal expression of the Nodal target genes lefty1 and lefty2.
source: Similarly, apelin receptor a and b single and double mutants also displayed normal expression of the Nodal target genes lefty1 and lefty2 (Figure 3B–C).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 3B-C.

claim: RNA-Seq analysis found no significant differences in Nodal target gene expression at any time-point prior to or during early gastrulation between wild-type and toddler mutants.
source: Second, we analyzed Nodal target gene expression by RNA-Seq at four time points prior to or during early gastrulation in wild-type and toddler mutants. We found no significant differences at any time-point in the expression of Nodal target genes (Dubrulle et al., 2015) or broadly across all genes (Figure 3D)(Figure 3—Source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by RNA-Seq data in Figure 3D.

claim: There were no significant differences in gene expression broadly across all genes between wild-type and toddler mutants prior to or during early gastrulation.
source: We found no significant differences at any time-point in the expression of Nodal target genes (Dubrulle et al., 2015) or broadly across all genes (Figure 3D)(Figure 3—Source data 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by RNA-Seq data in Figure 3D.

claim: Wild-type and toddler mutants show no significant difference in the ability to respond to exogenous Nodal.
source: Third, wild-type and toddler mutant embryos were injected at the one cell stage with increasing levels of Nodal mRNA and Nodal target gene expression was measured just prior to gastrulation using qRT-PCR. We found no significant difference in the ability of wild-type and toddler mutants to respond to exogenous Nodal (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by qRT-PCR data in Figure 4A.

claim: Wild-type and toddler mutants displayed Nodal target gene expression at the same frequencies after transplantation of cells expressing Nodal mRNA.
source: Fourth, cells expressing Nodal mRNA were transplanted into a host embryo and the host was assayed for Nodal target gene induction using in situ hybridization (Figure 4B). Wild-type and toddler mutants displayed target gene expression at the same frequencies and across the same distances (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by transplantation data in Figure 4.

claim: Wild-type and toddler mutants displayed Nodal target gene expression across the same distances after transplantation of cells expressing Nodal mRNA.
source: Wild-type and toddler mutants displayed target gene expression at the same frequencies and across the same distances (Figure 4C–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by transplantation data in Figure 4.

claim: The establishment of Nodal signaling is normal in toddler mutants.
source: These results indicate that the establishment of Nodal signaling is normal in toddler mutants.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on multiple assays of Nodal signaling in Figures 3 and 4.

claim: apelin receptor a and b gene expression resembles expression of the mesoderm markers fn1a and fascin, respectively.
source: Furthermore, apelin receptor a and b gene expression in wild-type embryos resembles expression of the mesoderm markers fn1a and fascin, respectively, and is dependent on signaling by the mesendoderm inducer Nodal (Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information supported by citation.

claim: The endodermal marker sox17 displayed increased expression in sox32 mRNA-injected embryos.
source: As expected, the endodermal marker sox17 displayed increased expression in sox32 mRNA-injected embryos or decreased expression in sox32 mutant embryos (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: The endodermal marker sox17 displayed decreased expression in sox32 mutant embryos.
source: As expected, the endodermal marker sox17 displayed increased expression in sox32 mRNA-injected embryos or decreased expression in sox32 mutant embryos (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 5A.

claim: The expression of mesodermal markers fn1a and ta increased upon loss of endoderm.
source: In contrast, the expression of mesodermal markers fn1a and ta or of apelin receptor a and b increased upon loss of endoderm (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 5 ).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 5A and supplement.

claim: The expression of apelin receptor a and b increased upon loss of endoderm.
source: In contrast, the expression of mesodermal markers fn1a and ta or of apelin receptor a and b increased upon loss of endoderm (Figure 5A and Figure 5—figure supplement 5 ).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 5A and supplement.

claim: apelin receptor b expression was retained at the site of internalization in embryos lacking endoderm, suggesting its expression is not ectodermal but mesodermal.
source: Furthermore, apelin receptor b expression was retained at the site of internalization in embryos lacking endoderm, suggesting its expression is not ectodermal but mesodermal (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding and inference from the study supported by data in Figure 5B.

claim: apelin receptor a and b are expressed in mesodermal progenitors.
source: These results indicate that apelin receptor a and b are expressed in mesodermal progenitors.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the sox32 manipulation experiments.

claim: Mesodermal cells moved more slowly in toddler mutants than in wild-type embryos.
source: We found that mesodermal cells moved more slowly in toddler mutants than in wild-type embryos (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by light sheet microscopy data in Figure 5D.

claim: toddler mutant mesodermal cells showed diminished animal pole-directed migration.
source: In addition, toddler mutant mesodermal cells showed diminished animal pole-directed migration, resulting in persistent vegetal and dorsal-ward migration during gastrulation (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by light sheet microscopy data in Figure 5E.

claim: toddler mutant mesodermal cells show persistent vegetal and dorsal-ward migration during gastrulation.
source: In addition, toddler mutant mesodermal cells showed diminished animal pole-directed migration, resulting in persistent vegetal and dorsal-ward migration during gastrulation (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by light sheet microscopy data in Figure 5E.

claim: Toddler signaling is required for proper animal-pole directed movement of mesodermal cells during gastrulation.
source: Taken together, these results indicate that Toddler signaling is required for proper animal-pole directed movement of mesodermal cells during gastrulation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the light sheet microscopy data in Figure 5.

claim: Lack of endoderm did not change the normal mesoderm dispersion in wild-type embryos.
source: We found that lack of endoderm did not change the normal mesoderm dispersion in wild-type embryos or the reduced migration in toddler mutants (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Lack of endoderm did not change the reduced migration in toddler mutants.
source: We found that lack of endoderm did not change the normal mesoderm dispersion in wild-type embryos or the reduced migration in toddler mutants (Figure 6A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: The mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants are independent of endoderm.
source: These results indicate that the mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants are independent of endoderm and suggest a direct role of Toddler signaling on mesoderm.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the toddler;sox32 double mutant data in Figure 6.

claim: Toddler signaling has a direct role on mesoderm.
source: These results indicate that the mesodermal cell migration defects in toddler mutants are independent of endoderm and suggest a direct role of Toddler signaling on mesoderm.
evidence: This is an inference based on the toddler;sox32 double mutant data in Figure 6.

claim: Mesodermal cells migrated normally in cxcr4a mutants.
source: We used Cas9-mediated mutagenesis to create a null mutant for cxcr4a (as described in Materials and methods) and observed that mesodermal cells migrated normally (Figure 7A–B)
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 7A-B.

claim: The most vegetal endodermal cells dispersed further animally in cxcr4a mutants than in wild type.
source: while the most vegetal endodermal cells dispersed further animally than in wild type, consistent with previous Cxcr4a morphant studies (Figure 7C–D) (Mizoguchi et al., 2008; Nair and Schilling, 2008).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 7C-D and consistent with previous studies.

claim: Mesodermal cell migration in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants was as reduced as in toddler single mutants.
source: As expected, mesodermal cell migration in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants was as reduced as in toddler single mutants (Figure 7A–B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 7A-B.

claim: Endoderm dispersion was increased in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants as compared to toddler single mutants.
source: Strikingly, however, endoderm dispersion was increased in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants as compared to toddler single mutants (Figure 7C–D).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 7C-D.

claim: The number of endodermal cells did not change in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants compared to toddler single mutants.
source: While endoderm migration was increased in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants, the number of endodermal cells did not change (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 7E.

claim: The reduced mesodermal cell migration in toddler mutants limits endodermal dispersion.
source: These observations indicate that the reduced mesodermal cell migration in toddler mutants limits endodermal dispersion and that Toddler signaling is not required for endodermal cell migration per se.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the toddler;cxcr4a double mutant data in Figure 7.

claim: Toddler signaling is not required for endodermal cell migration per se.
source: These observations indicate that the reduced mesodermal cell migration in toddler mutants limits endodermal dispersion and that Toddler signaling is not required for endodermal cell migration per se.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the toddler;cxcr4a double mutant data in Figure 7.

claim: Nodal signaling induces the expression of apelin receptor a and b in mesendodermal cells.
source: Nodal signaling induces the expression of apelin receptor a and b in mesendodermal cells, rendering them sensitive to Toddler peptide (Figure 5A–B)(Pauli et al., 2014; Tucker et al., 2007).
evidence: This is part of the model supported by data in Figure 5 and citations.

claim: Toddler signaling directly regulates animal-pole directed migration of mesodermal cells.
source: Toddler signaling directly regulates animal-pole directed migration of mesodermal cells (Figures 5 and 6)(Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is part of the model supported by data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: A Cxcr4a-regulated tether between endodermal and mesodermal cells allows Toddler signaling to indirectly affect endodermal cell migration.
source: A Cxcr4a-regulated tether between endodermal and mesodermal cells allows Toddler signaling to indirectly affect endodermal cell migration (Figure 7)(Mizoguchi et al., 2008; Nair and Schilling, 2008).
evidence: This is part of the model supported by data in Figure 7 and citations.

claim: Deshwar and colleagues reported that apelin receptor a and b double morphants appear to have a delayed onset of Nodal signaling.
source: Whereas Deshwar and colleagues reported that apelin receptor a and b double morphants appear to have a delayed onset of Nodal signaling, we find that toddler mutants as well as apelin receptor a and b single and double mutants establish Nodal signaling normally (Figure 3).
evidence: This describes a finding from a previous study that differs from the current study's findings.

claim: toddler mutants establish Nodal signaling normally.
source: Whereas Deshwar and colleagues reported that apelin receptor a and b double morphants appear to have a delayed onset of Nodal signaling, we find that toddler mutants as well as apelin receptor a and b single and double mutants establish Nodal signaling normally (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: apelin receptor a and b single and double mutants establish Nodal signaling normally.
source: Whereas Deshwar and colleagues reported that apelin receptor a and b double morphants appear to have a delayed onset of Nodal signaling, we find that toddler mutants as well as apelin receptor a and b single and double mutants establish Nodal signaling normally (Figure 3).
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 3.

claim: Toddler and/or the Apelin receptors may have independent functions.
source: First, it is possible that Toddler and/or the Apelin receptors have independent functions (Ho et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for differences between studies, supported by citation.

claim: Knockdown of the receptors via morpholinos might reveal a phenotype that is masked or compensated in the null mutants.
source: Second, although apelin receptor mutants and morphants have similar morphological defects (Deshwar et al., 2016), knockdown of the receptors via morpholinos might reveal a phenotype that is masked or compensated in the null mutants (Rossi et al., 2015; Wei et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for differences between studies, supported by citations.

claim: Morpholino injection may cause non-specific delayed development or toxicity.
source: Third, morpholino injection may cause non-specific delayed development or toxicity, as suggested by the epiboly defects seen in apelin receptor a morphants but not apelin receptor a mutants (Ekker and Larson, 2001; Kok et al., 2015; Deshwar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a speculative explanation for differences between studies, supported by citations.

claim: Toddler is a regulator of mesodermal cell migration.
source: Our study indicates that Toddler is a regulator of mesodermal cell migration and only indirectly regulates endodermal cell migration during gastrulation.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on multiple experimental results.

claim: Toddler only indirectly regulates endodermal cell migration during gastrulation.
source: Our study indicates that Toddler is a regulator of mesodermal cell migration and only indirectly regulates endodermal cell migration during gastrulation.
evidence: This is a main conclusion of the study based on multiple experimental results.

claim: Both endodermal cells and mesodermal cells migrate more slowly in the absence of Toddler signaling.
source: Accordingly, we find both similarities and differences in the role of Toddler signaling in the migration of endoderm versus mesoderm. Both endodermal cells (Pauli et al., 2014) and mesodermal cells (this study, Figure 5D) migrate more slowly in the absence of Toddler signaling.
evidence: This is a finding from the study and previous work, supported by data in Figure 5D.

claim: toddler mutant mesodermal cells have reduced animal pole-directed migration during gastrulation.
source: However, we find that toddler mutant mesodermal cells have reduced animal pole-directed migration during gastrulation.
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: Endodermal cells initially undergo a random walk, including animal pole-directed movement, in wild-type and toddler mutants.
source: This is in contrast to endodermal cells, which initially undergo a random walk, including animal pole-directed movement, in wild-type and toddler mutants (Pauli et al., 2014).
evidence: This is background information from previous work supported by citation.

claim: The intrinsic ability of endoderm to migrate without Toddler signaling is fully revealed in the abundant animal pole-directed migration of endoderm in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants.
source: The intrinsic ability of endoderm to migrate without Toddler signaling is fully revealed in the abundant animal pole-directed migration of endoderm in toddler;cxcr4a double mutants.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the toddler;cxcr4a double mutant data in Figure 7.

claim: The ability to undergo animal pole-directed migration is retained in endodermal cells but compromised in mesodermal cells in the absence of Toddler signaling.
source: Thus, the ability to undergo animal pole-directed migration is retained in endodermal cells but compromised in mesodermal cells in the absence of Toddler signaling.

claim: Toddler has an anti-apoptotic function.
source: Our work and others have suggested an anti-apoptotic function for Toddler (Ho et al., 2015)
evidence: This is based on findings from this study and previous work, supported by citation.

claim: RNA-Seq results in toddler mutants did not reveal major changes in gene expression during gastrulation.
source: Our RNA-Seq results in toddler mutants did not reveal major changes in gene expression during gastrulation (Figure 3)
evidence: This is a finding from the study supported by RNA-Seq data in Figure 3.

claim: Toddler's primary function may be post-transcriptional.
source: Our RNA-Seq results in toddler mutants did not reveal major changes in gene expression during gastrulation (Figure 3), suggesting that Toddler's primary function may be post-transcriptional.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation based on the lack of transcriptional changes in RNA-Seq data.

claim: In the absence of both Toddler and Cxcr4a signaling, endoderm migration is surprisingly normal.
source: In the absence of both Toddler and Cxcr4a signaling, endoderm migration is surprisingly normal.
evidence: This is an observation from the toddler;cxcr4a double mutant data in Figure 7.

claim: lefty1a145 is a null allele harboring a 13 base pair deletion that destroys a PshAI restriction enzyme site.
source: lefty1a145 is a null allele harboring a 13 base pair deletion that destroys a PshAI restriction enzyme site (Rogers et al. submitted).

claim: lefty2a146 is a null allele harboring an 11 base pair deletion.
source: lefty2a146 is a null allele harboring an 11 base pair deletion that was genotyped with allele-specific primers (Table 1)(Rogers et al. submitted).

source: The cxcr4a mutant line harbors a 433 bp deletion of a 1083 bp long coding sequence, generating a frameshift after the 28th amino acid and was genotyped with allele-specific primers (see Table 1 for gRNAs and primers).
